newsitem.title: UK: Mildly friendly tender boosts UK grain futures.
newsitem.headline: Mildly friendly tender boosts UK grain futures.

text.p: UK grain traders called the result of the last European Union (EU) tender of 1996 "mildy friendly" on Thursday.
The EU granted licenses for 397,500 tonnes of free-market soft wheat at 11.84 Ecus rebate and 237,500 tonnes of free-market barley at 28.99 Ecus rebate.
"The market is so thin that anything other than a zero rebate is going to be seen as friendly," said a trader.
Earlier LIFFE wheat futures had been supported by news that Iraq was to buy at least 100,000 tonnes of French wheat with oil revenue and by a weaker sterling.
At the close wheat futures were 1.10 to 0.10 stg up on a low turnover of 155 lots.
Most traded March last traded at 98.70 stg, 1.10 stg up with 55 lots against the position.
Barley finished 0.25 to 0.50 stg higher on turnover of 16 lots.
Most traded March finished with a last trade of 95.75 stg, 0.50 stg up and trading 10 lots.
Amsterdam milling wheat futures were neglected.
